thread:
Emma (Support): heads up — two enterprise customers hit a spike of repeated 429s this morning during a marketing campaign. They saw ~10k requests over ~40s and then sustained errors. Ticket escalated, asked for repro steps and whether default RPM/TPM + burst window are sane.

Raj (EngSRE): thanks, can you paste sample logs/headers from the requests? curious about the quota headers like X-RateLimit-* or any 5xx during the tail.

Emma (Support): pasted minimal log snippets below — redacted API keys. noticed a lot of `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` then 429s — no 5xx. Also some latency spikes ~1.6s per request right before throttles.

```
> POST /v1/generate 200 153ms X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 12 X-RateLimit-Reset: 1977654400
> POST /v1/generate 200 1.6s X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 X-RateLimit-Reset: 1977654405
> POST /v1/generate 429 0.3s X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 X-RateLimit-Reset: 1977654405
```

Mira (Product): are these customers on dedicated capacity or hosted? if hosted, did they use multiple API keys across devices or a single key? could be multi-tenant shock.

Emma (Support): hosted. they were using the same org key across many clients — looks like orchestrated from a scheduler hitting thousands of short queries.

Raj (EngSRE): ok — that screams burst exhaustion on a single key. We should reproduce with internal load test that mixes many short requests to stress-token-rate behavior + KV cache cold starts to hit latency. I can run a focused bench. Need a reproducible harness: mix of 50ms and 500ms mean response token sizes.

QA-bot: reproducibility checklist: 1) use 3 API keys (single-key, multi-key, mixed) 2) vary concurrency and inter-arrival to simulate scheduled spikes 3) capture X-RateLimit headers and p95/p99 latency 4) include canned prompt set (small vs. long) 5) measure token throughput and burst-drop counts.

Mike (EngInfra): also instrument quota window behavior — our rate windows are per-tenant rolling vs fixed-second buckets? we need to confirm to interpret the Reset header.

Raj (EngSRE): short notes: our current default per-org RPM = 3600, TPM = 60000? (we should double-check). Burst allowance is implemented as a short credit window (configurable), default burst multiplier = 2x for 10s. If customers do 3x sustained within 30s we will exhaust credits.

Emma (Support): customer wants a recommendation for safe defaults and a small troubleshooting playbook for SREs. Ideally we supply a repro they can run themselves and a list of mitigation steps.

Raj (EngSRE): plan: I'll run an internal benchmark this afternoon with the following matrix and post results here.

- Keys: [single-key heavy, multi-key spread (5 keys), multi-key spread (20 keys)]
- Request pattern: [burst 10s, 30s, 60s] with peak RPS values scaled to hit ~2x, 3x, 5x nominal RPM
- Payloads: [short (30 tokens), medium (250 tokens), long (1024 tokens)]
- Clients: concurrent connections 50/200/800 to simulate scheduler farms
- Measurements: 429 count, p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, X-RateLimit-* time series, CPU/GPU load on serving nodes

Mike (EngInfra): add bucketed histograms for connection queue depth and backend queueing latency. if we see head-of-line queuing it'll skew latency before 429s.

QA-bot: generating load harness snippet for run (curl-based emulation adapter).

```
# sample runner (pseudo)
for i in $(seq 1 $CONC); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} " -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":50}' &
done
wait
```

Raj (EngSRE): will also spin up a `wrk` + custom body generator to simulate token variance. tagging @Mike to collect infra metrics.

Emma (Support): for the playbook: first triage step: confirm whether the org is hitting a single key; second: check headers for Reset and Remaining; third: propose temporary mitigation like short rollout to client to spread requests across multiple keys or introduce jitter and backoff.

Mira (Product): from product POV we should consider updating docs to recommend multi-key for heavy scheduled workloads and a sample backoff jitter snippet. also argue for raising the default burst window if tests show common workloads exceed it.

Raj (EngSRE): early findings (quick local run): with single-key heavy burst (peak ~6k RPS for 20s) we hit Remaining=0 within ~7s and 429s spiked at 8s. multi-key (5 keys) smoothed but still saw per-key exhaustion when sustained >2x nominal. latency p95 shot up before 429s, indicating queueing.

```
# extracted header timeline (from bench)
t=0s X-RateLimit-Remaining: 90
t=5s X-RateLimit-Remaining: 2
t=7s X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
t=8s 429 count: 120
```

Mike (EngInfra): notable infra observation: serving node CPU climbed and request queue depth increased ~x3 before upstream throttles. we might be applying backpressure late.

Raj (EngSRE): implication: default burst multiplier 2x over 10s too small for some real campaigns; but increasing blindly increases risk of noisy-neighbor for shared hosted customers. we should calibrate safer defaults plus guidance.

Emma (Support): what concrete recommendations can we give to the customers now?

Raj (EngSRE): immediate mitigations to propose to customers:
- spread load across N keys (N=number of origin workers)
- add exponential backoff with randomized jitter on 429s (example snippet below)
- if on Dedicated, request quota bump or reserved capacity

```
# pseudo-backoff (JS)
const backoff = (attempt) => Math.min(2000 * Math.pow(2, attempt) + Math.random()*300, 30000);
```

Mira (Product): next product action: create a doc page "Scheduled-high-throughput best practices" and update Quickstart to mention multi-key and jitter for cron-driven workloads. add a faq entry on recommended RPM/TMP patterns.

Raj (EngSRE): internal action items:
- I will run full matrix bench and post CSV (ETA 6h) — tag `1977654900` for result artifact.
- Mike to collect serving node metrics during runs and flag queueing thresholds.
- Emma to send the support playbook to both customers with recommended mitigations.
- Mira to draft doc edits and coordinate with docs.

infra-bot: scheduled load job created: load-run-1977654321-raj (ETA 6h). :white_check_mark:

Emma (Support): thanks team — I'll reply to both customers with the short mitigation list and let them know we're running internal calibration. will include a sample jitter/backoff and offer temporary keys if they need to spread load quickly. :thumbsup:

Raj (EngSRE): will follow up with numbers. if the matrix suggests more conservative defaults (e.g., burst multiplier 1.5x over 30s, or default per-org RPM lowered), we'll propose a staged rollout with a beta flag for hosted customers to opt into higher burst allowances.

Mira (Product): agreed. please include regression tests so we don't accidentally increase noisy-neighbor risk.

Mike (EngInfra): FYI — if we add a per-tenant adaptive smoothing algorithm later, we can consider short-lived credit buckets replenished at token-level granularity instead of fixed windows. that's a medium-term infra project.

QA-bot: tagging results placeholder: results artifact -> s3://internal-loads/1977654321/results.csv (will be updated).

Emma (Support): closing loop for now — customers updated. will paste their responses when they confirm.

Raj (EngSRE): leaving running note: when bench completes I'll include the full raw traces + a condensed guidance sheet for support and product.

(End of thread)
